pages.drivingContext: on Edmonton's northwest edge, a short drive up St. Albert Trail from downtown
intro: St. Albert sits on Edmonton's northwest edge, along the Sturgeon River, and it has the housing stock to prove its age: mature streets with original trim, dated colour schemes and woodwork that rewards a careful repaint. Chris Lloyd Ltd works across the city — from downtown-adjacent neighbourhoods to the newer subdivisions off Ray Gibbon Drive.

The work is mostly interiors: repainting walls, ceilings and trim in homes that were last painted decades ago, plus the odd exterior refresh ahead of an Alberta winter. If you're in St. Albert and want a straight answer about what your project needs, get in touch.

pages.drivingContext: in Strathcona County, just east of Edmonton — about twenty minutes from downtown via the henday ring road
intro: Sherwood Park is Strathcona County's urban core, just east of Edmonton off Highway 16 and Highway 21. It's a community of family neighbourhoods and generous lots, which means a steady mix of work: bright repaints for busy households, refreshes ahead of listings, and repairs done properly rather than patched.

Chris Lloyd Ltd paints Sherwood Park interiors and exteriors year-round — walls, ceilings, trim, fascias and doors — with tidy prep and a clean finish. Reach out through the contact section on the main site for a quote.

pages.drivingContext: south of Edmonton on Highway 2, beside the international airport — roughly a twenty-five minute drive from downtown
intro: Leduc is south of Edmonton on Highway 2, next door to the international airport, and it has grown fast: newer subdivisions stacked around an older, well-kept core. Both sides of that mix are regular work — colour refreshes in newer builds where the builder-grade beige needs replacing, and careful prep-and-paint in mature homes.
Interior and exterior painting, drywall repair and renovation touch-ups are all on the table in Leduc. The contact form and details are on the main site.

pages.drivingContext: west of Edmonton on the Yellowhead (Highway 16), next to Stony Plain — about twenty-five minutes from downtown
intro: Spruce Grove sits west of Edmonton on the Yellowhead, beside Stony Plain, and like Leduc it pairs an established core with fast-growing new neighbourhoods. That means two kinds of jobs: repainting exteriors that have seen a few Alberta winters, and putting a personal finish on freshly built interiors that all arrived the same shade of grey.
Chris Lloyd Ltd handles interior and exterior painting plus small renovation work across Spruce Grove. Start at the main site's contact section to get a quote.
